cards.explanation: The answer is cities to live in, with pasturelands around them. The LORD tells Moses to have Israel give them from the inheritance the people will possess (Numbers 35:2). The Levites get homes and room for their herds and flocks. That fits what the LORD said earlier, that the Levites would receive no inheritance among the Israelites (Numbers 18:23-24). So the other tribes share what they have, and the Levites aren't left out.

The word is refuge. These are cities where a manslayer may flee (Numbers 35:6). A refuge is a safe place to run to, and six of the Levites' cities get that job. That's a lot of responsibility for a city that also has to find room for cows.

The answer is False. The text says the cities are given in proportion to each tribe's inheritance: “more from a larger tribe and less from a smaller one.” (Numbers 35:8) It's like everybody chipping in on the cookie order by how big their family is. Same rule for all, different amounts.

The cities of refuge are for someone who kills a person by accident. The LORD says they are “…so that a person who kills someone unintentionally may flee there.” (Numbers 35:11) These cities are for someone who never meant to take a life. It's a serious matter, and the LORD makes a place for it.

The answer is the assembly. The city of refuge keeps the avenger from reaching the manslayer first. His case goes before the assembly, so nothing gets settled on the road (Numbers 35:12). The city is where he stays safe until then.

The answer is False. Three cities of refuge are across the Jordan, and three are in the land of Canaan (Numbers 35:14). It's like putting three cookies on each side of the tray. Six cities, split evenly.

The answer is True. The six cities serve “…as a refuge for the Israelites and for the foreigner or stranger among them…” (Numbers 35:15). Anyone who kills a person unintentionally may flee there. The door isn't only for one group.

The answer is that he must be put to death. For each of these, iron, a stone of deadly size and a deadly object of wood, the LORD says the one who killed is a murderer, and “the murderer must surely be put to death.” (Numbers 35:16-18) It's a heavy part of the passage. The LORD is clear about it.

The answer is True. The text says, “The avenger of blood is to put the murderer to death; when he finds him, he is to kill him.” (Numbers 35:19) This is for the murderer, not for the one who killed by accident. That's why the difference matters so much in this passage.

The answer is True. Even a bare hand can do it. The verses just before name an iron object, a stone and a wooden object (Numbers 35:16-18), and then verse 21 adds that if in hostility someone strikes another with his hand and he dies, the one who struck him must surely be put to death, and he is a murderer. So no tool is needed in that case. It's a heavy part, and the text is clear.

The assembly is to protect the manslayer from the avenger of blood. When the killing was an accident, the assembly shields him (Numbers 35:25). Then the assembly brings him back to the city of refuge where he fled. He lives there until the death of the high priest.

The word is death. The manslayer “…must live there until the death of the high priest, who was anointed with the holy oil.” (Numbers 35:25) Only after that may he return to the land he owns (Numbers 35:28). He stays put until then.

The answer is False. The text says, “…then the avenger will not be guilty of bloodshed, because the manslayer must remain in his city of refuge until the death of the high priest.” (Numbers 35:27-28) The city is where he's protected. Outside it, that protection is gone.

The answer is more than one witness. The text says the murderer is put to death “…on the testimony of the witnesses. But no one is to be put to death based on the testimony of a lone witness.” (Numbers 35:30) One voice isn't enough for something this serious. It takes more than one.

The answer is never accept one. The LORD says, “You are not to accept a ransom for the life of a murderer who deserves to die; he must surely be put to death.” (Numbers 35:31) No payment changes that. That's about as clear as the text gets.

The answer is False. The text says, “Nor should you accept a ransom for the person who flees to a city of refuge and allow him to return and live on his own land before the death of the high priest.” (Numbers 35:32) So no buying a ticket home early. No payment shortens that stay, and the text is firm.

The word is blood. The text says, “…no atonement can be made for the land on which the blood is shed, except by the blood of the one who shed it.” (Numbers 35:33) It also says bloodshed pollutes the land. It's a weighty verse, and the answer is plain.

The reason the text gives is that He dwells among the Israelites. The LORD says, “Do not defile the land where you live and where I dwell. For I, the LORD, dwell among the Israelites.” (Numbers 35:34) The land matters because He lives among His people. Just before this, He says bloodshed pollutes the land (Numbers 35:33). I think that's a lot to take in, and it shows how seriously He treats life.
